full_text_en:
Western Trust Co., Ltd. v. Shaanxi Honghua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. et al. — Application for Reconsideration of Enforcement

【Ruling Summary】

Where a third party raises an objection based on claiming substantive rights to the subject property for the purpose of excluding compulsory enforcement against such subject property, that objection constitutes a third-party objection. Regardless of whether the basis for the third party's claim of substantive rights involves relevant legally effective judgments or rulings of other courts, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, in order to protect the legitimate rights of the third party and the parties to seek substantive relief through litigation.

Ruling of the Supreme People's Court on Enforcement Reconsideration

(2013) Zhi Fu Zi No. 11

Applicant for Reconsideration (Enforcement Applicant): Western Trust Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 232, Dongxin Street, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Zhaohui, Chairman of the Board.

Third Party (Objector): Shaanxi Transportation Property Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 300, Youyi West Road, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Xiaopeng, General Manager.

Enforcement Respondent: Shaanxi Honghua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 2, Gaoxin Road, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Li, Manager.

Enforcement Respondent: China Aviation Supplies Import and Export Corporation Northwest Company. Domicile: No. 296, Laodong South Road, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Tan Kejian, General Manager.

Enforcement Respondent: Shaanxi Provincial Transportation Workers' Technical Association Service Department. Domicile: No. 12, Yaowangdong, Xi'an, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Xiong Qiushui, Manager of the Service Department.

The applicant for reconsideration, Western Trust Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Western Trust Company), being dissatisfied with the Enforcement Ruling (2012) Shan Zhi Yi Zi No. 5 of the Shaanxi High People's Court, filed an application for reconsideration with this Court. After acceptance, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct review. The review is now concluded.

During the enforcement of the case concerning the dispute over a loan guarantee between the enforcement applicant Western Trust Company and Shaanxi Honghua Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., China Aviation Supplies Import and Export Corporation Northwest Company, and Shaanxi Provincial Transportation Workers' Technical Association Service Department (hereinafter referred to as the Transportation Technical Association), based on the legally effective Civil Judgment (2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 31 of the Supreme People's Court, the Shaanxi High People's Court, pursuant to property leads provided by the enforcement applicant Western Trust Company, issued the Enforcement Ruling (2011) Shan Zhi Hui Zi No. 16-4 on January 18, 2012, sealing up the properties located on the 12th floor (construction area 1,278.5 square meters) and the 6th floor (construction area 115.83 square meters) of Xi'an Science and Technology (Lihua) Building at No. 8 Gaoxin Road, Xi'an (hereinafter referred to as the subject properties). The third party, Shaanxi Transportation Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Transportation Property Company), raised an objection, requesting the lifting of the sealing-up order on the subject properties, on the grounds that: In June 2004, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Xi'an Intermediate Court) issued the Civil Ruling (2001) Xi Jing Zhi Zi No. 120-2, valuing the subject properties at RMB 6,888,513.78 and transferring them in satisfaction of a debt to the enforcement applicant in that case, the Transportation Technical Association. Later, the Transportation Technical Association transferred the subject properties to Shaanxi Road Science, Industry and Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Daoke Trade Company). The Xi'an Intermediate Court issued a Notice of Assistance in Enforcement (2001) Xi Jing Zhi Zi No. 120-3, requiring the High-tech Branch of Xi'an Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration to directly transfer ownership of the subject properties to Daoke Trade Company. After Daoke Trade Company's business license was revoked, the Shaanxi Provincial Department of Transportation, as the controlling unit of Daoke Trade Company, recovered the subject properties and handed them over to Transportation Property Company for possession and operation. Therefore, the subject properties have now been lawfully acquired by Transportation Property Company and no longer belong to the Transportation Technical Association. The sealing-up measure taken by the Shaanxi High People's Court was improper and should be revoked.

After review, the Shaanxi High People's Court found that Transportation Property Company's objection was well-founded and issued the Enforcement Ruling (2012) Shan Zhi Yi Zi No. 5, ruling as follows in accordance with Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China prior to amendment: The objection of Transportation Property Company is sustained. If dissatisfied with this ruling, an application for reconsideration may be filed with the Supreme People's Court within ten days from the date of service of this ruling.

Western Trust Company applied to this Court for reconsideration, arguing: Although Daoke Trade Company's business license was revoked, it has not undergone liquidation or completed the cancellation of its business registration, and its legal personality as an enterprise still exists. Transportation Property Company is not the owner of the subject properties and does not have the standing to raise an enforcement objection. The Enforcement Ruling (2012) Shan Zhi Yi Zi No. 5 of the Shaanxi High People's Court is erroneous and should be revoked.

Opinion of the Court: Where a third party raises an objection based on claiming substantive rights to the subject property for the purpose of excluding compulsory enforcement against such subject property, that objection constitutes a third-party objection. Regardless of whether the basis for the third party's claim of substantive rights involves relevant legally effective judgments or rulings of other courts, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (i.e., the original Article 204), in order to protect the legitimate rights of the third party and the parties to seek substantive relief through litigation. In this case, the third party, Transportation Property Company, relying on the relevant civil ruling and the notice of assistance in enforcement issued by the Xi'an Intermediate Court, claimed that it had lawfully acquired the subject properties and that the Shaanxi High People's Court should no longer enforce them as property of the Transportation Technical Association. This clearly constitutes an effort to exclude enforcement by asserting substantive rights, and thus is a third-party objection. It should be reviewed and an objection ruling made in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (i.e., the original Article 204). Since this third-party objection is unrelated to the Civil Judgment (2005) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 31 of the Supreme People's Court, which serves as the basis for enforcement, if the third party or the parties are dissatisfied with the objection ruling, they should resolve the matter by filing a lawsuit in the enforcing court. The Enforcement Ruling (2012) Shan Zhi Yi Zi No. 5 of the Shaanxi High People's Court applied Article 202 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China prior to its amendment, granting the third party and the parties the right to apply for reconsideration to the higher-level court, which constitutes an error in the application of procedural law. By reference to Article 170(1)(iv) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

1. Revoke the Enforcement Ruling (2012) Shan Zhi Yi Zi No. 5 of the Shaanxi High People's Court.

2. Remand the case to the Shaanxi High People's Court for a new review and ruling in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Huang Jinlong

Judge: Fan Xiangyang

Acting Judge: Yang Chun

August 8, 2013

Clerk: Wei Dan

[Brief Introduction of the Presiding Judge]
Huang Jinlong, Senior Judge: Born in 1965; Master of Laws. Appointed as Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2000.
